chronologyIntro: A journey from the steppe to Anatolia. Explore the atlas’s selected events in chronological order.
sourcesIntro: Behind every story is a source. The atlas’s narratives draw on the reference works and institutional publications below.
aboutIntro: Seyri Cihan is an independent hobby project exploring how Turkic and Turkish history connects with time and geography.
methodBody: The boundary layer uses Ottoman Empire geometries from CShapes for January 1 of each year from 1886 to 1914. Generalized state boundaries are not a complete depiction of wartime fronts, effective control, or all dependent territories. Extrusion height is only a visual distinction. No boundaries are drawn outside this coverage, including in 1453; another year's boundaries are never substituted. CShapes data is provided under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for noncommercial use.
scopeBody: This first edition connects selected turning points from the Göktürks to the proclamation of the Turkish Republic. It does not claim to be a complete history of all Turkic peoples and regions. Period labels are editorial navigation aids.
principles: Explore with curiosity. Go deeper with sources.
principlesBody: Choose a year, open an event on the globe and read its context. Source links in each story help you continue your research. The chronology provides access to every event without the 3D globe.
sourceNote: References for event narratives are separate from the source of boundary geometries. Boundaries come from CShapes; the selected record's validity dates and license link appear in the atlas boundary dossier. Encyclopedia links are not treated as verification of boundary geometry.
mapNote: The irregular map relief is a source-informed approximate context area, not an exact boundary or the event's full geographic reach.
